mechanism: Overweighting vivid individual evidence while ignoring prior statistical prevalence.
countermeasure: Compute the prior probability first before updating on new test results.

mechanism: Drawing conclusions strictly from visible successes while missing failed or filtered-out cases.
countermeasure: Ask whose data never made it into the sample before extrapolating.

mechanism: Continuing an unpromising investment solely because prior irrecoverable resources were spent.
countermeasure: Evaluate forward expected value as if deciding cleanly from zero today.

mechanism: Over-attributing others' behavior to stable character while excusing our own via situational pressures.
countermeasure: Check what situational constraints another person faced first.

mechanism: Judging event probability by how effortlessly vivid examples come to mind rather than real frequency.
countermeasure: Replace gut recall with actual incidence rates or denominators.

mechanism: When a proxy measure becomes a target metric, it ceases to serve as a reliable measure.
countermeasure: Pair quantitative targets with qualitative audits and counter-metrics.

mechanism: Letting an arbitrary initial number pull subsequent estimates excessively toward that starting value.
countermeasure: Write down an independent bottom-up estimate before viewing any anchor.

mechanism: Believing after an outcome unfolds that it was predictable all along (\"knew it all along\").
countermeasure: Keep pre-decision prediction logs with explicit probabilities.

mechanism: Searching for, interpreting, and remembering evidence in ways that favor pre-existing beliefs while discounting contradictory data.
countermeasure: Deliberately list falsifying criteria and steelman the strongest opposing argument.

mechanism: Underestimating task durations, costs, and risks by modeling best-case execution instead of historical completion data.
countermeasure: Use reference class forecasting based on similar past projects (the outside view).

mechanism: Experiencing equivalent losses roughly twice as intensely as gains, inducing excessive caution or desperate risk-seeking to avoid realizing a loss.
countermeasure: Frame choices in terms of total final state rather than isolated gains or losses.

mechanism: Preferring the current baseline state disproportionately even when switching costs are smaller than the expected benefit of change.
countermeasure: Ask: "If I were not already committed to this option today, would I actively choose it?"

mechanism: Misjudging one's own competence at low skill levels because the expertise needed to perform well is the same expertise needed to spot errors.
countermeasure: Seek objective external benchmarks, blinded feedback, and structured post-mortems.

mechanism: Judging a detailed combination of events as more probable than one of its broader constituent events.
countermeasure: Check subset logic explicitly: adding constraints can never raise true probability (P(A ∩ B) <= P(A)).

mechanism: Expecting independent random trials to even out in the short run after a streak of identical outcomes.
countermeasure: Verify whether trials are statistically independent before updating odds from recent history.

mechanism: Attributing causal stories to natural rebound toward average performance following an extreme outlier measurement.
countermeasure: Separate random noise from real intervention effects using control groups or multi-sample baselines.

mechanism: Reaching opposite choices on identical expected outcomes depending on whether options are phrased as gains ("90% survive") or losses ("10% die").
countermeasure: Restate every high-stakes choice in both gain and loss frames before deciding.

mechanism: Overestimating how closely other people notice, scrutinize, and remember our minor mistakes or appearance.
countermeasure: Remind yourself that others' attention is predominantly occupied by their own concerns.

mechanism: Placing inflated subjective value on plans, products, or ideas simply because we invested personal labor assembling or creating them.
countermeasure: Have uninvolved reviewers evaluate the output without knowing who built it.

mechanism: Weighting the latest events or data points far more heavily than equally diagnostic long-term evidence.
countermeasure: Plot full historical series and enforce pre-defined review windows before reacting.

mechanism: Demanding a much higher price to give up something we own than we would ever pay to acquire that identical item.
countermeasure: Compare against fair replacement cost and ask whether you would buy the item today at your asking price.

mechanism: Judging the quality of a past decision solely by its eventual result rather than the soundness of the information and odds available at decision time.
countermeasure: Audit decision memos strictly using the evidence and probabilities known before the outcome occurred.
